title: Food Rations
text: A little while later, I arrived at the town that was the Lazy Pig’s territory.

But… this town looks familiar… Huh! The Lazy Pig is Elena—the one who was with me in the first world! I feel like Father mentioned her name several times, but I thought it was just a pig with the same name. This is the town where that traitor was put in charge of the shop.

Ugh… How could I not have realized that this Lazy Pig was actually Elena, the traitor? I’m sure she’ll betray me again the moment things get tough. I’ll have to figure out how to kill her discreetly so Father doesn’t find out.

…No, on the other hand, if her situation doesn’t get dire, she might actually be a useful asset? After all, the Lazy Pig’s abilities are actually quite decent. She’s given Father plenty of advice—on peddling, guiding people to safety during the waves, and cultivation methods for the bio-plant. In a way, you could say she has abilities I lack. Given her capabilities, it would be a shame to just get rid of her so easily.
You could say that making someone not want to betray you is a form of power in itself.

In that sense, my Father from the first world serves as a good example. I’ve heard he commands a crew of unsavory characters—monster merchants, thieves, and the like—whose names I can’t even bring myself to say. They’re honest about pursuing their own interests, after all. If Father’s position were to weaken, they’d cast him aside in a heartbeat. Perhaps the key is to make such people want to remain on your side.
Of course, I can’t afford to keep incompetents around. At best, I’ll just make convenient use of them as Father’s pawns. Besides, if they betray me, I’ll execute them without hesitation.

Now, back when I was on the run in the first world after the Spirit Tortoise Incident—when I was planning to trust Lazy Pig and join forces with him—this was the place I headed for. My father crept up on me and tried to drag me back to the castle, didn’t he? After that, I escaped through a portal.
“Oink.”

The Lazy Pig seemed annoyed as he walked into the shop and appeared to be talking about something in the back. After that, my father headed toward the mansion in town and rented a nearby field. According to my father, the official reason is that it’s a field managed by the Lazy Pig’s family.
As soon as my father planted the seeds in the fields, they grew before our very eyes. Red, familiar fruits began to ripen. The first phase of the plan was a success.
Soon, farmers hired by the Lazy Pig’s household came to harvest the fruits and load them onto a wagon.
“I hear the merchant from Elena’s place is going around selling all sorts of things. Well, I think it’ll probably be fine, but please be careful.”
“Oink…”

After the Lazy Pig gave orders to his subordinate farmers, we set out on a journey to distribute food. Of course, we also sold medicine in between food deliveries. However, when we took food to impoverished areas like the villages in the southwest, it sold like hotcakes.

However, my father said it was fine to provide food for free or on credit to those who were poor and struggling to put food on the table. Since we also accepted barter or exchanges for medicinal herbs, all sorts of goods were loaded onto the wagons. The number of wagons pulled by Yuki-chan and Kou has increased, and everyone is delighted. After all, the Filolial-samas do like heavy wagons.

By this time, Luna-chan had grown quite a bit and had taken on the form of a Filolial Queen. I suppose it’s just her personality, but she’s built more robustly than the other Filolial-samas. And while she was navy blue at first, her color scheme is now white with navy accents. Color-wise, she looks like a different shade of Filo-tan. It’s about time she became an angel.
“Luna-chan, I really hope you’ll take on the form of an angel.”
“Motoyasu-kun, we’re on a public road here… Wait, Luna-chan, don’t just go along with this!”

Thanks to my wish, Luna-chan—who had been walking outside the carriage—transformed into an angel. …Huh? Father is hurriedly covering Luna-chan with a towel. Then he tells her to get back in the carriage.
“…Luna… nice to meet you.”
“Um, we don’t have a spare carriage yet, so it’s fine.”
“…Really?”
Her build and appearance are just as youthful as Yuki-chan’s and the others’. Compared to Sakura-chan, there’s definitely a big difference. I took another good look at Luna-chan’s angelic form.
First off, her eye color is navy blue. Her eyes are a deep navy blue, like the ocean at night. That hasn’t changed.
Next is her hair color. It’s a silky, shimmering silver. It absorbs the sunlight and sparkles beautifully.
The color scheme is quite different from how Filolial-sama has looked up until now.
As for her hairstyle—tastes vary, of course—but my Father asked Luna-chan what she liked and let her choose. It seems Luna-chan prefers to tie it up on one side.
“She looks a bit different compared to Yuki-chan, Kou, and Sakura-chan, doesn’t she?”
“That’s true.”
“Her hair color doesn’t really match the color scheme of her Filolial form.”
“Did we do anything different this time?”
“Hmm… Well, she’s been eating chimera meat lately, but we’ve been eating it too…”
I have no idea. However, there was also a difference between Filo-tan’s angel form and her Filolial form. What could be causing this?
“…Weird?”
“It’s not weird. It’s just… different, you know?”

It seems Luna-chan isn’t very good at talking. A lot of her conversations end with just one word. Sakura-chan is also on the quiet side, but she still answers when asked, and she seems to like singing. Luna-chan, on the other hand, tends to keep her comments short in general. That’s just her personality.
“…Huh…”
“Boo…”
“Ah, yeah. You’re a lot like Elena, Luna-chan. Don’t copy her, okay?”
“…I’m not copying her.”
She’s the cool type, isn’t she? Luna-chan seems to prefer acting quietly. When she encounters monsters, she likes to strike from behind.
“But… why is her hair color different from Sakura-chan’s and the others’ when she’s in her angel form…? Well, Sakura-chan’s eye color is different from the others’ too, though.”
That’s true. Come to think of it, Filo-tan has her own unique differences as well.
“Iwa… Keel, I’m going to sleep on Luna’s tummy.”
When night falls, Luna-chan in her Filolial form plops down, beckons her Father over, and has him pat her tummy.
“Luna-chan’s belly? That looks warm!”
Keel approaches and leans against Luna-chan’s belly. Luna-chan gazes at him with very gentle eyes.
“Whoa. It’s super soft!”
“Kou is ready to welcome Keel-kun, too!”
With that, Kou opens his mouth wide.
“I have no intention of going inside! Give it a rest!”
Keel barks at Kou, baring his canine teeth.
“Luna-chan seems to like having her belly patted.”
“…Yeah. Keel-kun is cute.”
Luna-chan gives Keel a tight hug. Hmm, it seems she likes Keel in a different way than she likes Kou. Liking Keel as a puppy is a very girly side of her.
“Cute, my foot! He’s cool, isn’t he?”
“…Luna, I want to be like Keel-kun. I want to be small and go ‘peep peep.’”
“I think you’re cute enough as it is…”

Luna’s feathers fluffed up softly, making her look like a chick. However, perhaps because her body is a bit on the large side, and with those long legs, her proportions are a bit off. Well, Filolial-sama is equally adorable, though.
“I think your angel form is just as cute as Keel-kun’s.”
“…Luna, I want my true form to be cute… I want to go ‘cheep cheep’…”
“Hmm… Everyone’s so unique. I wonder if I could get along with Lars-chan…?”
That’s true. That panda Beastman seemed to like cute things and didn’t mind dressing up. She and Luna-chan seem like they’d get along well.
Tate and Party’s Good Deeds Points: 20 (7)
